title: Accept-Language Header Matcher
statement:
Select supported locale tags that satisfy an HTTP-style `Accept-Language` preference list, ordered by client preference.

Contract
- `header` is a non-null comma-separated string of requested language tags (for example `"fr-CA, en, *"`). Surrounding spaces around each tag are ignored, and blank entries are skipped.
- `supported` is a non-null list of distinct, non-blank supported tags in server priority order (for example `["en-US", "en-GB", "fr-CA"]`).
- Matching is case-insensitive, and every tag in the returned list must use the exact spelling from `supported`.
- Evaluate tags in `header` from left to right:
  - A tag with a region subtag (contains `'-'`, like `en-US`) matches only the exact same tag in `supported`.
  - A base language tag (no `'-'`, like `en`) matches any supported tag equal to it or starting with `<base>-`, in `supported` order.
  - The wildcard `"*"` matches all remaining tags in `supported`, in `supported` order.
- Never return duplicates: once a supported tag has been added, later preferences skip it.

Examples
- `matchLanguages("en-US, fr-CA", ["fr-CA", "en-GB", "en-US"])` returns `["en-US", "fr-CA"]`.
- `matchLanguages("en, fr-CA", ["fr-FR", "en-GB", "en-US", "fr-CA"])` returns `["en-GB", "en-US", "fr-CA"]`.
- `matchLanguages("de-DE, *", ["en-US", "fr-FR"])` returns `["en-US", "fr-FR"]`.
hints: Pre-index the supported tags into two maps keyed by lowercase strings: exact tag -> original tag, and base language (prefix before '-') -> ordered list of original supported tags.
Track already-selected supported tags in a HashSet so exact matches, base-language matches, and '*' never emit duplicates.
When '*' appears, append every supported tag not yet in the seen set and stop scanning further preferences. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: header | supported1, supported2, for example: en, fr-CA | fr-FR, en-GB, en-US, fr-CA
sampleInput: en, fr-CA | fr-FR, en-GB, en-US, fr-CA
